functions.name: capability_request
functions.description: Ask for a capability that an installed add-on module provides, without naming the module. Only capabilities a module slot marks client-callable are available (language.explain: put a finding into plain words; language.advise: investigate and recommend). Needs the grant `capability:NAME` (for example capability:language.advise), which in 2.5.0 only a static bearer client can hold (a person signed in with OAuth cannot; see docs/CONFIGURE.md). Read-only: the module has no network and the server hands it only your input. Every call is audited by digest and size (never by content); a call that cannot be audited is refused. Rate limited per client. The answer is MODEL-GENERATED and UNVERIFIED, labeled so in the result; language.advise is advisory only and nothing is executed. With no provider you get capability_state=capability_unavailable and a reason_code (no_provider, provider_unhealthy, agent_unavailable). Other refusals: bad_request, not_client_callable, rate_limited, audit_unavailable, module_error. Reference: docs/MODULES.md.

functions.name: kernel_session_open
functions.description: System 5.7.1 only. Open or rejoin the resident Probot/Fred/Data kernel for this conversation. It stores only a compact plan summary and never transfers tools, credentials, approvals, or private context. Returns `continuity`, exactly one of: bound (this key was already an alias of a live kernel), adopted (no key match; a keyless reconnect of the same client rejoined a DIFFERENT live kernel), superseded (this key's own kernel had expired -- it was closed, replaced, and its plan carried forward into the replacement), or opened (nothing existed for this key; a genuinely new kernel). THIS CALL ONLY FILLS AN EMPTY PLAN and never overwrites an authored one. It now says so: `written` is false and `plan_write` is "refused" when the plan you sent was not stored, and the returned plan_summary is then the RETAINED plan, not yours. To CHANGE an authored plan, call kernel_plan_update.

functions.name: ladder_status
functions.description: Every answer carries `release_ladder` (task #992 S3b): MATCHES or DIFFERS against the ladder THIS server release shipped, every difference named, and the one command that repairs it (install/migrate.sh --ladder-only). That is the reference now (decision #660). Also: Report one factory's live convergence verdict against Commons, the canonical ladder home (task #823, decisions #552/#555). Computes the factory's current manifest and asks Commons's own gate-read function whether it matches canonical content right now -- returns converged or drifted, never invented locally. Not read-only: the reachable path causes Commons to upsert its one row for this factory in ladder.convergence_registry, as a recorded side effect of the check, not a write to any table this call's own argument names. If Commons cannot be reached, this never fabricates a verdict -- it reports state=DEGRADED from the factory's own read-through cache (ladder.v_convergence_cache_status) with the cache's real age. BLOCKED is not a value this tool can return; that vocabulary does not exist in the cache view. Every non-refused answer also carries `kernel` (tasks #849/#867), computed first and independently of convergence: `kernel.floor.verdict` is AT_FLOOR / BELOW_FLOOR / NO_FLOOR / UNKNOWN against the min_kernel_version Commons's payload declares, with the local version read from both ladder.pull_kernel and fn_kernel_version() and their agreement; `kernel.engine_instrument.state` is PRESENT AND READABLE / PRESENT BUT UNREACHABLE / ABSENT / UNMEASURED for ladder.v_kernel_engine_drift, measured by a real SELECT as the factory role (never to_regclass); `kernel.engine_verdict` rolls its rows up to ALL_MATCHED / DRIFTED / UNMEASURED. `kernel.floor.green` requires AT_FLOOR and not behind the publisher's current kernel.

functions.description: Administrators only. Queues the install of ONE add-on module by its slot id (docling, advanced-logic, mom). The caller must be a signed-in person whose account tier is admin (a service credential or a non-admin person is refused with person_required or admin_tier_required). Every call is audited before the request is written, and a call that cannot be audited is refused. Answers module_install_state=queued with a job_id, or refused with a reason_code (admin_tier_required, person_required, unknown_module, already_installed, already_in_progress, spool_unavailable, audit_unavailable). Progress and the reason for a failure are in module_status.catalog. Reference: docs/MODULES.md.

functions.name: ocr_folder_process
functions.description: Governed OCR (task #884). Runs the configured OCR runner (RapidOCR on ONNX Runtime) over every eligible file in a NAMED intake folder from server config -- `folder` is a name such as proposals_ocr, never a path. Images (png/jpg/tif/bmp/webp) and scanned PDFs. Originals are hashed before and after and never modified. Output goes only to that folder's configured output directory, in a new per-run directory: a .txt and .ocr.json sidecar per file plus manifest.json. Returns processed files (page count, mean confidence, source sha256, engine and model versions, timestamps, sidecar paths), skipped files with reasons (unsupported_type, symlink, file_too_large, run_*_limit), errors, and the manifest path. Refused unless the folder is granted to this factory (and, if configured, this client). Unconfigured: returns reason_code ocr_not_configured. Details: omatic_guide(topic="ocr"). Choose the path with `engine`: reader (the Reader module only: Office, PDF, images, HTML; a Reader failure is an error, never a quiet fallback), ocr (RapidOCR only: images and PDFs, the Reader is never called), vision (read-only inventory of files and page counts; read pages with vision_page_get), all (Reader plus RapidOCR, the default). The Reader reads images and PDFs with its own OCR, so reader and ocr do not produce identical text for the same scan.

functions.name: omatic_guide
functions.description: Documentation this server hands out about itself. topic='operating' (default) is the operating guide: the full tool list, how to start a factory, how retrieval is governed, and what a refusal means. topic='architecture' is the architecture description in industry terms — the three-tier vector memory model, the embedding contract, hybrid retrieval by reciprocal rank fusion, the governance and grant model, the audit trail, and the known gaps. Read 'architecture' when you need to explain or evaluate this system rather than operate it. topic='slate' is the slate.ops/1 operation set: every operation slate_proposal_create accepts, its required and optional arguments, and every reason_code it can refuse with. Read 'slate' before composing a proposal. topic='templates' lists the page templates the server ships; 'project-headquarters' and 'server-closet' explain those two pages; 'upgrade' is the recipe book for a factory upgrade that did not come out clean. 'blueprint' is the factory Blueprint (how a factory is built, governed, certified, installed and upgraded); read it before changing a factory, and 'blueprint-install-upgrade' before fixing an upgrade.

functions.name: proposal_vault_append
functions.description: Adds 1 to 100 base64 attachments (each at most 50 MiB, the request at most 200 MiB) to a batch that ALREADY exists in the file vault (batch_not_found otherwise: proposal_vault_transfer_batch creates a new one). Files are selected by the same rule as ingest and transfer_batch: a type the vault does not admit, an extraction product (*.extracted.*) or a packet-manifest.json is listed under `skipped` in the answer and in the manifest, never added. Each file is copied and verified by SHA-256, then a NEW sibling manifest `custody-manifest.append-<UTC timestamp>-<n>.json` records them; the original custody-manifest.json and every earlier manifest are never rewritten. A name that already exists in the batch with OTHER bytes is refused (exists); with the SAME bytes it is `already_present` only if an earlier manifest recorded THOSE bytes for that name (otherwise exists, with a custody_mismatch warning). A file no manifest records (an orphan) is adopted only when the custody log holds an append record that named it, or an ADMINISTRATOR sends adopt_orphans=true (orphan_not_adoptable, adopt_orphans_requires_admin otherwise). A reserved name (the two custody manifest shapes, any dot component) is refused reserved_name, a name the vault cannot handle later (backslash, control character, trailing space or dot, over 255 bytes a name or 1024 a path) bad_path, a symlink on the path symlink_refused, a name repeated in the request duplicate_in_request; all are checked before the first byte is written. Any granted writer may append to any batch (append is not folder-scoped). A folder with no original custody manifest needs `adopt=true` (adopt_required) and is marked adopted in the manifest. Audited FIRST (audit_unavailable), and a pending record naming the planned files and their sha256 is written to the custody log BEFORE the first byte is published (custody_write_failed refuses). If it stops part-way (or the server is killed), what was published is recorded in an incomplete manifest and the answer is append_incomplete with `published` and `unwritten`; send the SAME request again and it resumes. For a large file use proposal_vault_upload_start with append=true. Any granted read_write client.

functions.name: proposal_vault_delete
functions.description: Any client granted the vault with write permission. Moves ONE vault file to the server's trash, a sibling of the vault root that list and ingest never see, with a manifest row (original path, sha256, size, actor, time). Nothing is copied or destroyed: proposal_vault_restore puts it back, and proposal_vault_purge removes it permanently once it is old enough. The audit record is written FIRST; if it cannot be, the call is refused with audit_unavailable and nothing moves. Refuses a symlink, a path outside the vault, a folder and a trash on another filesystem. Reason codes: not_authenticated, read_only, bad_path, not_found, symlink_refused, not_a_file, audit_unavailable, cross_device, trash_move_failed, trash_write_failed, changed_during_delete, protected_custody_file (custody manifests, hidden metadata and the audit log are never deletable), delete_rate_exceeded (200 per client per hour), proposal_vault_not_configured.

A reserved name, a symlink, a type the vault does not admit and an extraction product are listed under `skipped`.

functions.name: proposal_vault_list
functions.description: Read-only. Lists the files in the configured file vault, or in one packet folder of it, with bytes and (by default) SHA-256 for each. `hashes=false` skips the SHA-256 and reads no file body at all: use it to look around a large vault. Custody manifests (custody-manifest.json and every custody-manifest.append-*.json) are listed; the server's own folders at the vault root (the custody event log, the failure records) are not. A symlink is never followed or listed. ONE audit line is written per call, with a count. `packet` is a folder relative to the vault root, never an absolute path. Refused unless the vault is configured for this connection and this client was granted it. Unconfigured: reason_code proposal_vault_not_configured.

functions.name: proposal_vault_organize
functions.description: Moves or renames ONE file in the file vault to a new vault-relative path, creating missing folders. Any client granted the vault with write permission (not read_only) may use it, to any folder in the vault. The customer boundary is on the data: a file never moves into a batch recorded for a different customer (customer_mismatch), and a file that has a customer never moves to a place that records none (the vault root, a folder with no custody manifest, a batch with no customer); a file with no customer recorded moves freely except into a batch that has one. The customer is the one named at intake (the `customer` argument of transfer_batch, ingest, upload_start and append), never guessed from a folder name. It never overwrites (exists), never follows a symlink (symlink_refused), never leaves the vault (bad_path), never crosses a filesystem (cross_device), and never touches the vault's own metadata: custody manifests (custody-manifest*), names with a dot component, the server's own folders and the audit log (protected_custody_file for a source, reserved_name for a destination). Audited FIRST: if the audit record cannot be written the call is refused (audit_unavailable) and nothing moves. The move is recorded (from, to, sha256, size, actor and persona, time) in the vault's append-only custody event log, crash-safe: an interrupted move is settled on the next call BY HASH (a file with other bytes at the destination is flagged organize_mismatch in `warnings`, never marked done). No custody manifest is edited. To undo, organize the file back (`undo` in the answer). `reason` is recorded as its sha256 and length ONLY; the text is never written to any log (it can hold PHI), so keep a ticket id out of it and in your own ticketing system. Reason codes: not_authenticated, not_granted, wrong_connection, read_only, password_change_pending, customer_mismatch, bad_path (a name the vault cannot handle later is refused at creation), bad_reason, same_path, not_found, not_a_file, symlink_refused, exists, parent_not_directory, cross_device, protected_custody_file, reserved_name, audit_unavailable, custody_write_failed, custody_log_unreadable, move_failed, changed_during_move, proposal_vault_not_configured.

functions.name: proposal_vault_purge
functions.description: Person-bound administrators only (a service credential is refused admin_required). PERMANENT. Removes trash entries older than the minimum age (7 days by default, configurable, never under 1 hour; a call may raise it, never lower it), at most purge_cap (50) per call. DRY RUN by default: it lists what it would remove, including the OCR output and staged copies derived from the same sha256, but only when no other copy of that content exists. It acts only with dry_run=false AND confirm=true AND the plan_token the dry run returned (60 minutes, once). Per client: 100 items per rolling 24 hours (purge_budget_exceeded). A purge that leaves anything server-owned behind ends purged_with_residue. Even a dry run is not read-only: like the listing it first settles any half-done delete or restore. Each purge writes a tombstone (sha256, size, original path, time, actor) for Data, and reports what it removed and what it could NOT reach: evidence rows, embeddings and ledger rows belong to Data. Audited first; audit_unavailable refuses with nothing removed.

functions.name: startup

One round trip: the connections this client was granted AND the factory's startup card (identity, corpus, retrieval state, roster, governance, open work, READY/DEGRADED/BLOCKED with a reason). Replaces calling connections_list and then factory_query, which cost two round trips at ~4.5s each. Omit `connection` when exactly one is granted; with several, it returns the list and asks rather than guessing which factory you meant. Read `state` first and believe nothing else until it passes; `unmeasured` names fields this factory genuinely cannot report, which is not the same as zero. PASS `conversation_key`: startup opens this conversation's resident kernel, and without a key it can only address one by guessing -- it will join an existing kernel but will not create one, and the card reports DEGRADED.

It names candidates; it does not decide. Wording cannot see an umbrella task that absorbed this work, so read the matches. The server also flags likely duplicates automatically when a new task is embedded. connection defaults to this server's own factory.

Groups are built around hub tasks so one heavily cited task does not merge everything. Pass task_id for that task's blast radius (its linked tasks, the lanes they sit in, and the groups that contain it) before planning a fix (SOP-023). connection defaults to this server's own factory.
